details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> llama : report compute graph reallocations during inference (#30329) Add an optional ggml_backend_sched_realloc_callback that user code registers with ggml_backend_sched_set_realloc_callback to be notified when the buffers reserved for a graph are not sufficient and have to be reserved again. The callback reports whether the backend assignments and the graph size changed since the previous scheduling. llama_context registers the callback when creating the scheduler (wrapped into the new llama_context::sched_new helper) and treats the reallocations that follow a change of the backend assignments as expected, counting the rest by graph size - unchanged or changed from the previously scheduled graph. Both counters are reported on one line in the perf stats. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next </details> **Website:** - <https://llama.app> **Attestations:** - <https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/attestations/55042647> **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](

details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> metal : fix mul_mat_id with duplicate ids (#30373) * metal : fix mul_mat_id limits and kernel name * metal : fix mul_mat_id with duplicate ids kernel_mul_mm_id_map0 assumed at most one match per token and a fixed capacity of ne21 entries per expert, which produced wrong or dropped output rows and could overflow into the slice of the next expert when the ids contain duplicates. build a compact per-expert list of the (token, slot) entries instead: - pass 1 counts the entries of every expert, thread 0 computes the offsets of the expert slices (tpe now holds [base, count]) - pass 2 writes the entries with one unconditional store per token (conditional stores of divergent lanes are very slow), the dummy value of the tokens without a match lands on a padding slot of the slice that is never read - duplicates are handled by a rare branch - kernel_mul_mm_id reads the base/count of its expert and loops over the entry tiles that do not fit into the grid The ids buffer is sized as n

details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> graph: pad the KV dimension of the no-cache attention to 256 (#30416) The no-cache path builds a [n_tokens, n_tokens] mask and passes K and V unpadded, so FLASH_ATTN_EXT sees K->ne[1] == n_tokens. The CUDA kernels for head size 512 require a multiple of FATTN_KQ_STRIDE, so the op falls back to the CPU for most lengths, and the -fa auto probe (1 token) disables flash attention for such models. Pad the mask like llama_kv_cache::get_n_kv and pad K and V with zeros up to the KV dimension of the mask. clef builds its own causal mask and pads it the same way. </details> **Website:** - <https://llama.app> **Attestations:** - <https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/attestations/55199687> **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11576/llama-b11576-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) [DISABLED](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/23780) - [macOS Intel (x64)](https://github.com/
